summary: src/26-vehicles.js was rewritten for v3, keeping VT, vehicleTop() and every collision value unchanged. Every vehicle type now has a real model at two levels of detail (LOD 0 near, LOD 1 far): sedan, taxi, van, delivery van with hazard lights, bus, cable car, tram and road-works barriers. Bodies are lofted (rounded plan and sides, wheel arches, separate inset glass behind rubber seals). Bumpers, lamps, grilles, plates, door handles, mirrors and wipers are added; tyres have tread and sidewall detail on 5-spoke alloys or steel wheels. They share one MeshPhysicalNodeMaterial: clearcoat paint with metal flakes, per-instance colour (metallic or solid), panel seams, tinted glass with a faint cabin and HDR head/tail lamps that bloom. Blinkers run on the city clock, plates and signs come from a generated atlas, and the material opts into SSR. All city vehicles (traffic and the 224 parked cars) are drawn by K.vehicles' own LOD pools, instanced per type: near, near-shadow proxy, far with shadows, and distant without shadows. Slots are assigned in onBeforeRender after the frame's updates, so a drawn car always matches its collision box. The city's own traffic meshes are hidden and only record poses. On the final code, the WebGL 2 e2e suites act2, regress2 and v3 passed 25/25, plus the Moyen budget target. On WebGPU the suite passed 6/6, run just before a last tweak of lamp brightness constants. ./build.sh passes. The models look clearly better than v2's boxes at the old v2 viewpoints (shots/final-v2-vs-v3.png). Nothing was committed.

Update the K.vehicles paragraph in the SPEC3 Foundation notes. Vehicles now use their own MeshPhysicalNodeMaterial (kinds 30-51, with 30 and 31 keeping their meaning) instead of cityMaterial({vehicle:true}). New API: buildLOD(type, lod) and stats(). The vehicles draw their own instanced pools in K.city.group (veh-near/shadow/far/dist-*). addTo() registers parked cars, so K.city.stats().buildTris.parked is 0.
Optional: add an act2 e2e check that K.vehicles.stats() is built, all 8 types are hooked and the pools hold instances. The pending Moyen budget target can become a check() (it passes for Act 2).
Optional (25-city.js comment only): bakeParked's comment still says the parked cars are baked into the street chunks.
known_issues: Wheels do not turn (static rims, as in v2).
When a vehicle changes LOD pool, its new slot can carry one frame of wrong motion vectors (TRAA / motion blur). Slots stay stable while a car keeps its LOD, so this happens rarely and at 16-170 m.
The sedan silhouette is held by vehicleTop(): a long flat roof from z -0.95 to 0.6 at 1.45 m, which gives a slightly long greenhouse.
The far cable car (LOD 1) is a plain-box version; the far tram and bus are coarse lofts.
In daylight the head and tail lamps bloom strongly at very close range (tuned down; still bright on Ultra).
The regress2 Act 1 lawn-seam check is flaky (world area, not vehicles).
